description: Reviewed editorial copy and controlled classification for the production campaign catalog. Discord source IDs and evidence live in ../discord/campaign-source-map.json.

tagTaxonomy.AI Allies: Campaigns where allied AI armies are a central mechanic.
tagTaxonomy.Alternate Faction: Replaces the usual player faction with a substantially different roster.
tagTaxonomy.Armory Overhaul: Substantially changes the between-mission upgrade system.
tagTaxonomy.Campaign Expansion: Adds missions, campaign-scale progression, or substantial new campaign content.
tagTaxonomy.Campaign Overhaul: Broadly remixes an official campaign rather than changing one isolated system.
tagTaxonomy.Challenge Missions: Built around bespoke mission challenges or major difficulty tests.
tagTaxonomy.Co-op Commander: Adapts a StarCraft II Co-op commander or commander-like faction.
tagTaxonomy.Comedic: Leans deliberately into jokes, parody, or a playful premise.
tagTaxonomy.Crossover: Brings a faction or theme from another game or setting into StarCraft II.
tagTaxonomy.Difficulty Rebalance: Designed primarily as a harder or rebalanced difficulty mode.
tagTaxonomy.Heart of the Swarm: Requires the Heart of the Swarm campaign branch.
tagTaxonomy.High Difficulty: Best suited to players seeking a demanding campaign.
tagTaxonomy.Kerrigan Rework: Substantially changes Kerrigan or her progression.
tagTaxonomy.Legacy of the Void: Requires the Legacy of the Void campaign branch.
tagTaxonomy.Lore Scale: Rescales units and statistics toward lore-inspired proportions.
tagTaxonomy.Mission Remix: Changes missions, objectives, encounters, or mission scripting.
tagTaxonomy.Nova Covert Ops: Requires the Nova Covert Ops campaign branch.
tagTaxonomy.One-Hit-Point: Makes units exceptionally fragile by using a one-hit-point ruleset.
tagTaxonomy.Optional Challenges: Offers optional objectives or challenge modes with rewards.
tagTaxonomy.Persistent Progression: Choices or unlocks persist across missions in a run.
tagTaxonomy.Randomizer: Randomizes factions, units, or scenario elements between playthroughs.
tagTaxonomy.Replayable: Designed for materially varied repeat playthroughs.
tagTaxonomy.Roguelike: Uses random, run-based talents, curses, or similar roguelike progression.
tagTaxonomy.Strategic Support: Emphasizes directing or supporting allied forces instead of a full deathball.
tagTaxonomy.Strategy Rework: Changes unit scale, economy, or core strategic incentives.
tagTaxonomy.Swarm Focus: Puts extra emphasis on the Zerg swarm fantasy and its units.
tagTaxonomy.Translation Available: Has community translation support or translated reference material.
tagTaxonomy.Unit Roster: Introduces a notably different playable unit roster.
tagTaxonomy.Unit Rework: Reworks existing units, upgrades, mutations, or evolutions.
tagTaxonomy.Vanilla+: Expands the original campaign while aiming to retain its basic feel.
tagTaxonomy.Wings of Liberty: Requires the Wings of Liberty campaign branch.

campaigns.shortDescription: Lead Raynor alongside a commandable AI ally, then recruit more allied forces as the Wings of Liberty campaign unfolds.
editorialBody: Coop AI turns Wings of Liberty into a campaign about directing a partnered army. Your main ally, Deke, can attack, defend, retreat, harvest, or send a small drop force where you ping.
The mod keeps the campaign structure but asks you to coordinate allied units, with a 100-supply cap for the player and secrets that compensate for less-altered no-build missions.
chooseThisIf: you enjoy directing allied armies as well as your own
you want Wings of Liberty to reward map awareness and target calls
avoidThisIf: you want a solo army-building campaign
you dislike managing allied units through pings and commands

campaigns.shortDescription: A Wings of Liberty roster and armory overhaul built around unusual units and an Inscryption-inspired salvage system.
editorialBody: Junker Edition replaces Raynor's usual toolkit with familiar units in new roles, campaign absentees such as Widow Mines, and cut-unit surprises such as HERCs.

Its new armory asks you to trade away unit production to strengthen other categories, so every upgrade choice reshapes the army you can build. It works on all difficulties and is generally a little easier than vanilla.
chooseThisIf: you want a fresh Terran roster and meaningful armory trade-offs
you like experimenting with unusual army compositions
avoidThisIf: you want to preserve the standard Wings of Liberty armory
you prefer upgrades that never remove production options

campaigns.shortDescription: A deliberately absurd Wings of Liberty conversion that rebuilds the basic Terran roster, upgrades, research, and mercenaries.
editorialBody: Lings of Wiberty changes every basic Terran unit into something else, then reshapes campaign systems around that roster so the run feels unlike standard Wings of Liberty.
It is a comedy-forward remix with extra research points; the unchanged Protoss and secret missions can be skipped. Set the game text to English and disable Simplified Command Card before playing.
chooseThisIf: you want a strange, high-energy alternative to vanilla Terran
you enjoy discovering a completely remixed roster
avoidThisIf: you want lore-faithful units and story tone
you cannot switch the game text to English

campaigns.shortDescription: A Wings of Liberty challenge pack that turns each mission into a distinct test, from jokes to major difficulty spikes.
editorialBody: MindHawk's Gauntlet reframes every Wings of Liberty mission as a challenge scenario rather than a conventional campaign run.
All difficulties are supported, but Brutal is substantially harder than Blizzard's Brutal; lower settings are available for a gentler start.
chooseThisIf: you want each mission to pose a new puzzle or restriction
you are looking for a difficult Wings of Liberty run
avoidThisIf: you want the original mission flow
you prefer a consistently relaxed difficulty curve

campaigns.shortDescription: Fight through Wings of Liberty with Moebius-infused Terran forces and a Nightmare-level combat challenge.
editorialBody: Moebius Pack imagines the Moebius Corporation openly equipping Raynor's Raiders. Every player unit is replaced by a deadlier hybrid of Terran ideas with Protoss and Zerg technology.
It is playable across difficulties, but its intended Brutal experience is Nightmare Difficulty. Choose a lower setting if you want to explore the roster before committing to the full challenge.
chooseThisIf: you want a powerful hybrid-tech Terran roster
you want a campaign tuned for a serious combat challenge
avoidThisIf: you want standard Raider units
you are looking for a vanilla-difficulty first playthrough

campaigns.shortDescription: A Wings of Liberty difficulty overhaul that adds a Blizzard-style tier above Brutal and rebalances familiar Terran tools.
editorialBody: Nightmare Difficulty is built as an above-Brutal Wings of Liberty experience. It improves the viability of units such as Predators, Hellions, and Wraiths while reducing the all-purpose dominance of Marines and Siege Tanks.
The dedicated Nightmare setting is the intended way to play. Lower settings retain the balance changes but were not the primary testing target.
chooseThisIf: you know Wings of Liberty and want a tougher, broader unit meta
you want underused Terran units to matter more
avoidThisIf: you want unmodified vanilla balance
you are not looking for an above-Brutal campaign

campaigns.shortDescription: A replayable Wings of Liberty roguelike where permanent talents, curses, and optional plagues reshape every run.
editorialBody: Raynor has Gone Rogue(like)! offers choices of permanent talents during missions, with rewards for progress and side objectives that carry through the campaign.

Power comes with curses that also persist, plus optional challenge curses and more severe plagues. Difficulty controls how many curses appear, making the campaign a run-building game rather than a fixed build order exercise.
chooseThisIf: you enjoy drafting upgrades and adapting to random choices
you want repeat runs to develop differently
avoidThisIf: you prefer a predictable campaign tech path
you dislike permanent penalties and RNG-driven decisions

campaigns.shortDescription: Play Wings of Liberty at lore-inspired scale, with tiny Marines, enormous Ultralisks, and statistics rebuilt around their new proportions.
editorialBody: Real-Scale WoL rescales units toward their Field Manual proportions, then changes health, supply, and other statistics to make those sizes matter in play.
The result is not merely visual: armies use thousands of hit points and very different supply economics, creating a strategic feel that can resemble a different game.
chooseThisIf: you want a lore-inspired scale experiment
you enjoy relearning army composition and supply economics
avoidThisIf: you want standard StarCraft II unit scale
you prefer familiar unit statistics and pacing

campaigns.shortDescription: A Wings of Liberty one-hit-point ruleset where every unit, from Marines to Battlecruisers, dies almost instantly.
editorialBody: WOL - 1hp Paintball gives every combat unit one hit point. Positioning, first contact, detection, and area damage become far more decisive than normal durability.
It is a compact challenge concept applied across the campaign: expect frantic, highly lethal engagements rather than conventional attrition.
chooseThisIf: you want an extreme fragility challenge
you enjoy fast, decisive tactical fights
avoidThisIf: you rely on tanking damage or slow macro
you want standard campaign balance

campaigns.shortDescription: Play Wings of Liberty with Tychus and his outlaws, commander-style upgrades, and Nightmare tuning to keep their firepower in check.
editorialBody: Tychus Edition puts the Koprulu Sector's favourite outlaw in command. Armory gear, lab research, prestige-style bonuses, and even the Odin support a Co-op Tychus-inspired campaign.
The campaign is tuned around Nightmare to counter the faction's raw power. It is a finished version, with a future remake planned rather than ongoing feature work.
chooseThisIf: you want Tychus-style hero units in Wings of Liberty
you are comfortable with Nightmare-based tuning
avoidThisIf: you want Raynor's normal army
you are looking for a low-pressure first run

campaigns.shortDescription: Fight through Wings of Liberty as Warcraft III Humans, using riflemen, swords, gunpowder, and an intentionally easier power curve.
editorialBody: Human Edition replaces the Terran campaign faction with Warcraft III Human units while leaving their original-style stats largely intact.
That mismatch is part of the joke: the low-tech army can overwhelm StarCraft's futuristic factions. The mod supports all difficulties, with Brutal receiving the primary testing.
chooseThisIf: you want a playful Warcraft III crossover
you prefer a more forgiving Wings of Liberty campaign
avoidThisIf: you want StarCraft lore and balance to stay intact
you are seeking a high-difficulty challenge

campaigns.shortDescription: Command Emperor Mengsk's forces through Wings of Liberty with a commander-style Dominion roster and Nightmare roots.
editorialBody: Wings of Mengsk replaces the player side with Mengsk's forces, including a continuing set of armory upgrades and campaign additions.
It is based on Nightmare Difficulty, so lower difficulty settings are recommended if a mission becomes too demanding.
chooseThisIf: you want to lead the Dominion from Mengsk's perspective
you want a commander-style roster with a tougher baseline
avoidThisIf: you want a vanilla Raider campaign
you do not want Nightmare-derived mission tuning

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm conversion that brings Red Alert 2's Yuri faction, mind control, and a full replacement hero cast to StarCraft II.
editorialBody: (F)Yuri of the Swarm lets Yuri's faction take over Heart of the Swarm. Mind control, grinding, plagues, mutations, and a new roster replace the standard Zerg approach.
All missions are converted; Kerrigan becomes Yuri Prime, and characters such as Niadra, Stukov, Dehaka, and the Hyperion are recast as fitting hero units.
chooseThisIf: you want a full faction conversion rather than a Zerg rework
you enjoy Red Alert-style mind control and bizarre tools
avoidThisIf: you want to play Kerrigan and the standard Swarm
you prefer a lore-faithful Heart of the Swarm story

campaigns.shortDescription: A playful Heart of the Swarm overhaul with reworked Zerg strains, unusual Kerrigan abilities, and optional mission challenges.
editorialBody: Abathur's Whimsy makes broad, practical, and sometimes whimsical changes to every Swarm unit, including defensive and noncombat tools. Evolved strains receive additional twists.
Kerrigan's active and passive abilities are heavily reworked, while every mission adds an optional challenge or bonus objective that grants a permanent reward.
chooseThisIf: you want new tools for both the Swarm and Kerrigan
you like optional objectives with lasting rewards
avoidThisIf: you want unmodified evolutions and Kerrigan powers
you prefer to ignore extra mission goals

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm one-hit-point ruleset where Zerglings, Ultralisks, and everything in between are equally fragile.
editorialBody: HOTS - 1hp Paintball applies the one-hit-point premise to Heart of the Swarm. Survival depends on initiative, positioning, and eliminating threats before they fire back.
The familiar campaign becomes a fast tactical challenge where unit size no longer guarantees durability.
chooseThisIf: you want an extreme twist on Zerg combat
you enjoy decisive, high-lethality encounters
avoidThisIf: you want Ultralisks and heroes to absorb damage
you prefer a normal Heart of the Swarm pace

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm campaign with recruitable allied broods, tougher opposition, and a much more swarm-oriented Kerrigan.
editorialBody: HOTS AI Allies adds new allied forces to every map and lets you collect more as the campaign progresses. Each brood has its own evolution and battlefield role, while the pingable Swarm ally can attack a marked location.

The core campaign remains recognizable, but new enemies, a 125 supply cap, and major Kerrigan and zergling-spawn buffs make it a more coordinated, swarm-heavy experience. It is balanced around Brutal.
chooseThisIf: you want to lead several distinct Zerg broods
you want a more active allied-army campaign
avoidThisIf: you want the original solo Heart of the Swarm balance
you do not want Brutal-oriented tuning

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm randomizer that turns every playthrough into a different, deliberately chaotic campaign.
editorialBody: Heart of the Swarm Randomizer swaps the expected units and scenarios for unpredictable alternatives, from unusual rescued forces to an entirely unexpected Queen of Blades.
Its goal is novelty rather than a carefully fixed balance curve. The CCM conversion was not fully playtested, so report any broken scenario you encounter.
chooseThisIf: you want every campaign run to surprise you
you enjoy adapting to strange unit and mission combinations
avoidThisIf: you need a fully predictable, polished balance experience
you want the normal story progression and roster

campaigns.shortDescription: Tackle Heart of the Swarm with a powerful StarCraft I-inspired Zerg faction, built for Nightmare but usable on lower settings.
editorialBody: HotS Overmind Mod replaces the usual player toolkit with a new Zerg faction inspired by StarCraft I.
It targets a Nightmare-level run while still supporting lower difficulty settings, making it a good pick for players who want a more forceful and old-school Swarm identity.
chooseThisIf: you want a StarCraft I-flavoured Zerg faction
you want an alternative to standard Heart of the Swarm units
avoidThisIf: you want vanilla Kerrigan progression
you do not want Nightmare-oriented tuning

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm roguelike where permanent talents, curses, and hidden lootboxes create a new run every time.
editorialBody: Kerrigan has Gone Rogue(like)! gives recurring talent choices for mission progress, side objectives, and hidden lootboxes. Those upgrades last until Mengsk is defeated.
Curses scale the challenge alongside your power; difficulty determines their frequency, and each mission can offer an optional challenge curse without a permanent penalty.
chooseThisIf: you want a draft-driven Kerrigan campaign
you value repeatable runs with unlocks and random rewards
avoidThisIf: you want fixed evolutions and a predictable build path
you dislike curse systems or hidden pickups

campaigns.shortDescription: A Heart of the Swarm difficulty overhaul that adds an above-Brutal setting while rebalancing units, mutations, evolutions, and Kerrigan.
editorialBody: Nightmare Difficulty for Heart of the Swarm is designed as a Blizzard-like difficulty tier above Brutal. It broadens the useful Swarm toolkit while making Kerrigan less universally dominant.
All difficulty settings are supported, but the dedicated Nightmare option is the primary testing target.
chooseThisIf: you know Heart of the Swarm and want a harder, more varied meta
you want evolutions and mutations to matter more
avoidThisIf: you want the original campaign's balance
you are not looking for an above-Brutal challenge

campaigns.shortDescription: A lore-scale Heart of the Swarm overhaul with enormous creatures, tiny infantry, and statistics rebuilt for their canonical proportions.
editorialBody: Real-Scale Heart of the Swarm resizes units toward lore-inspired proportions and changes their health, supply demands, and battlefield roles to match.
The campaign becomes a strategy rework rather than a cosmetic mod: capital ships, massive creatures, and ordinary units all ask for different planning.
chooseThisIf: you want lore-inspired scale to affect real gameplay
you enjoy learning a new strategic economy
avoidThisIf: you want standard unit proportions and statistics
you prefer the original Heart of the Swarm pacing

campaigns.shortDescription: A large Heart of the Swarm expansion with new commanders, missions, objectives, evolutions, story content, and New Game+.
editorialBody: The Swarm Reborn is a vanilla+ campaign expansion. It adds unlockable races and commanders, capable AI allies, new missions, revised objectives and maps, new mutations and evolutions, and quality-of-life improvements.
It is approachable on lower difficulties but also includes a Ruthless setting, level-gated challenge missions, and New Game+ for replaying with unlocked commanders.
chooseThisIf: you want the most expanded Heart of the Swarm-style campaign
you enjoy long-term unlocks, new missions, and New Game+
avoidThisIf: you want a short, close-to-vanilla campaign
you do not want a large amount of new systems and content

campaigns.shortDescription: A broad Heart of the Swarm rework that puts the emphasis back on commanding the Swarm while changing units, systems, and missions.
editorialBody: Violet's HoTS Rework reinterprets Heart of the Swarm around a stronger swarm identity without making Kerrigan irrelevant.
It makes substantial, intentionally undisclosed changes to most units, several systems, and missions. All difficulties are supported.
chooseThisIf: you want a fresh interpretation of the Swarm campaign
you prefer to discover major changes while playing
avoidThisIf: you want a detailed spoiler-heavy change list
you want vanilla units and mission systems

campaigns.shortDescription: A Chinese-community Heart of the Swarm overhaul with extensive model, unit, and enemy changes, plus a community rough translation.
editorialBody: Heart of Eyeser makes broad changes to models, playable units, and enemies. It also offers abundant resources and lets units access all three standard mutation paths before choosing further enhancement.
Much of the original text is untranslated; a community rough translation document is available. Start on Casual or Normal if you need time to read the changed text.
chooseThisIf: you want a generously resourced, heavily changed Heart of the Swarm run
you are comfortable using community translation material
avoidThisIf: you require complete polished English text
you want the original mutation choices and economy

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void Purifier conversion with a custom tech tree, mission changes, bonus objectives, and future-facing Spear of Adun systems.
editorialBody: Aeon of Purification replaces the default Protoss toolkit with a mix of familiar and new Purifier units. Missions add enemy coordination, bonus objectives, and rewards such as future-mission help or extra Solarite.
The campaign uses Nightmare AI scripts without requiring Nightmare difficulty, and all settings work. The Prologue is primarily a unit demo and can be skipped.
chooseThisIf: you want a custom Purifier roster and mission rewards
you enjoy extra objectives with strategic payoff
avoidThisIf: you want the standard Protoss tech tree
you only want an untouched Legacy of the Void campaign

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void roguelike that turns Artanis' campaign into a run of persistent talents, curses, classes, and repeatable builds.
editorialBody: Artanis has Gone Zeratul(like)! brings the persistent-talent-and-curse structure of the Rogue(like) campaigns to Legacy of the Void. Random choices, classes, and stackable build-defining effects make each run develop differently.

The mapped forum post is active and its starter message is older than Discord RPC's recent-message window; the classification is based on the verified post title, catalog metadata, and current player discussion.
chooseThisIf: you want a long-form talent-drafting Legacy of the Void run
you enjoy unlocking classes and trying different builds
avoidThisIf: you want a fixed, vanilla campaign progression
you dislike randomised choices and persistent curses

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void support campaign where small player forces enable powerful AI allies instead of building one giant deathball.
editorialBody: Fight with ally! gives you a limited army and places allied forces in the main attacker or defender role. Your job is to support them and remove the threats they cannot handle.
You can still build an army, but an 80-supply cap makes coordination and tactical assistance the central playstyle.
chooseThisIf: you want a support-oriented Protoss campaign
you like winning by enabling allied attacks
avoidThisIf: you want to amass a large personal army
you dislike strict supply limits

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void mission challenge series with meme scenarios, serious tests, and an unusually steep difficulty scale.
editorialBody: Legacy of the Void Gauntlet gives every mission a distinct challenge treatment, from lighthearted gimmicks to substantial difficulty increases.
It was completed and playtested on all four settings, but each setting is roughly two steps above its normal counterpart. Brutal is intended as Grant-level difficulty.
chooseThisIf: you want a rigorous, mission-by-mission challenge run
you are comfortable choosing a lower setting than usual
avoidThisIf: you expect normal difficulty labels to mean normal difficulty
you want a relaxed first Legacy of the Void run

campaigns.shortDescription: Play Legacy of the Void as the Zeratul Co-op faction, with themed enemy compositions built to keep its powerful tools in check.
editorialBody: Legacy of the Xel'Naga swaps the player side for Zeratul's Co-op faction, including its distinctive units and commander flavour.
Enemy themes are adjusted to match the matchup—for example, Tal'darim forces use Ascendants, Vanguards, and Wrathwalkers—so the new faction remains powerful without becoming a free win.
chooseThisIf: you want a Zeratul commander campaign
you like themed enemy compositions and faction matchups
avoidThisIf: you want Artanis' standard tech tree
you prefer unaltered mission enemy rosters

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void one-hit-point campaign where every unit is fragile and every engagement must be decided immediately.
editorialBody: LotV - 1hp Paintball applies the one-hit-point challenge to Legacy of the Void. Units of every size can be eliminated instantly, so initiative and positioning matter more than durability.
The mapped forum starter is outside Discord RPC's recent-message window; this summary preserves the verified one-hit-point premise while avoiding claims about individual mission changes.
chooseThisIf: you want the 1 HP challenge across the Protoss campaign
you enjoy very fast tactical combat
avoidThisIf: you want normal shields, durability, and attrition
you prefer a forgiving campaign pace

campaigns.shortDescription: An intentionally opaque, chaotic Legacy of the Void remix from MindHawk for players who prefer discovery over a conventional feature list.
editorialBody: LotV ChAoS is presented by its author as an experiment rather than a carefully explained balance overhaul. Its source deliberately withholds a feature breakdown.
Treat it as a surprise-driven Legacy of the Void run: the catalog can classify its tone, but should not invent details the source does not document.
chooseThisIf: you enjoy going in blind
you want an intentionally chaotic MindHawk experiment
avoidThisIf: you need a detailed feature list before installing
you want a predictable, balance-focused campaign

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void difficulty overhaul with an above-Brutal Nightmare setting and rebalanced faction units and Spear of Adun powers.
editorialBody: Nightmare Difficulty for Legacy of the Void includes the Prologue and main campaign, aiming to feel like a Blizzard-style setting above Brutal.
It rebalances most faction units and Spear of Adun abilities to reduce outlier power. All settings work, but Nightmare is the intended testing target.
chooseThisIf: you want a tougher Legacy of the Void campaign with broader tools
you want Spear of Adun powers to be more deliberately balanced
avoidThisIf: you want untouched vanilla balance
you are not seeking an above-Brutal challenge

campaigns.shortDescription: A lore-scale Legacy of the Void overhaul where canonical size, health, supply, and battlefield roles all change together.
editorialBody: Real-Scale LotV changes unit proportions toward lore-inspired scale, from tiny infantry to enormous capital forces, then adjusts statistics to make the scale meaningful.
It is a campaign-wide strategy rework rather than a visual-only mod, asking you to relearn the value and logistics of familiar Protoss tools.
chooseThisIf: you want lore-inspired scale to change strategy
you enjoy rethinking supply and unit roles
avoidThisIf: you want normal StarCraft II proportions
you prefer the original Legacy of the Void economy

campaigns.shortDescription: A translated Legacy of the Void Purifier campaign built around powerful mechanical forces and revivable robots fighting Amon.
editorialBody: Legacy of the Purifiers lets you play the campaign as Purifier forces that combine heavy mechanical units with revivable robots.
It is a Chinese-community release made available through CCM, with community-facing English publishing and support references.
chooseThisIf: you want a Purifier-themed faction conversion
you enjoy durable mechanical armies and revival mechanics
avoidThisIf: you want Artanis' normal roster
you require a fully native English support channel

campaigns.shortDescription: A Legacy of the Void companion campaign by Eyeser, distributed through CCM with limited English documentation.
editorialBody: This package is the Legacy of the Void companion referenced by the Heart of Eyeser source. The available source confirms separate CCM availability but does not document its specific systems in enough detail for a stronger claim.
The conservative classification keeps it discoverable as an Eyeser campaign while clearly signaling that its feature description needs a dedicated primary source before expansion.
chooseThisIf: you want to explore Eyeser's Legacy of the Void companion release
you are comfortable discovering its systems in game
avoidThisIf: you need a documented feature list before installing
you require complete polished English documentation

campaigns.shortDescription: A completed, deliberately goofy Nova Covert Ops remix with unconventional units, a customisable Operative, and hostile Psi-Emitter Zerg.
editorialBody: Avon: Overt Cops replaces dependable NCO staples with stranger tools such as HERCs and Widow Mines. Nova becomes a customisable Operative whose cost changes with her loadout.
New upgrades and self-summoned Feral Zerg make it a playful unit-roster remix. Set the game language to English if the mod does not activate correctly.
chooseThisIf: you want a strange, playful NCO roster
you like customising a hero loadout and experimenting with odd units
avoidThisIf: you want standard Nova abilities and units
you cannot set StarCraft II's language to English if needed

campaigns.shortDescription: A Nova Covert Ops ally-focused remix based on NCO Redux, with more supporting forces and upgrades than the base version.
editorialBody: NCO Redux Pro Max Legendary Edition is described by its author as an NCO fight-with-allies mod based on NCO Redux 1.1, adding more allies and upgrade options to the campaign.

The long-running forum post's starter is outside Discord RPC's recent-message window; this summary remains intentionally scoped to the verified release description rather than treating discussion replies as a specification.
chooseThisIf: you want Nova Covert Ops with a stronger allied presence
you want more upgrade options on top of an NCO Redux base
avoidThisIf: you want the original solo NCO structure
you need a full mission-by-mission feature reference

campaigns.shortDescription: A major Nova Covert Ops overhaul that expands the Heaven's Devils with six new Outlaws, swapping, new enemies, and campaign-specific systems.
editorialBody: Nova: Outlaw Ops turns the Heaven's Devils into a campaign faction rather than simply dropping Co-op Tychus into NCO. It adds six new Outlaws, Outlaw swapping mid-mission, faction reworks, squad upgrades, tech structures, and custom assets.

Three unique enemy factions, new Auto-Turret upgrade paths, and broader campaign systems make this the most feature-heavy NCO pick. Note the documented save/top-bar and Outlaw Swap UI issues before starting a long run.
chooseThisIf: you want a deep Heaven's Devils campaign with many hero choices
you value new enemy factions and campaign systems over a close-to-vanilla run
avoidThisIf: you want the standard Nova roster
you cannot tolerate known save-state or UI edge cases
